38.0.s.en: 1. God challenges Job to answer His questions

38.0.0.en: 1 Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said, 2 "Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge? 3 Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.

38.0.1.en: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said [1]:

38.0.2.en: Some see that the Hebrew word translated here "whirlwind" differs from the one used for the storm in the previous chapter. In the previous chapter it points to a state of agitation, turbulence, uproar and violent upheaval, whereas here it points merely to a storm that fills Job's mind with a sense of awe and reverence for the greatness of God. As God spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai amid thunder and lightning (Ex 19:16-19), so He spoke with Job as a sign of the greatness of His majesty (Ps 18:9-13; Hab 3:3-6; Ps 50:3-4).

38.0.3.en: Although God appeared to Job in order to commend and justify him before those present, yet without partiality He revealed to him his weaknesses, and wished to remove from him his murmuring and complaint. For in God's tenderness toward man, He gives him countless blessings after He directs him so that his errors and weaknesses may be removed from him.

38.0.4.en: * When Job lost all his wealth, when he lost his children, everything began to work against him. But since he loved the Lord, all the evils that befell him worked for his good (Job 42:9-17). What befell his body prepared him for the crown of heaven (Job 7:5). Before the time of trial God had never spoken with him as a friend with his friend (Job 38:1; 42:9). So let the catastrophe come, let trials fall, as long as Christ comes after the calamity!

38.0.5.en: St. Jerome * What then of Him who answered Job out of the whirlwind and the cloud, slow to chastise and swift to help, who does not allow the rod of sinners to rest upon the lot of the wicked (Ps 3:25) lest the righteous learn evil?

38.0.6.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Someone may ask: Why did God speak with Job through the whirlwind?

38.0.7.en: First: He feared for Job lest he fall into pride because of the praise that He would give him publicly, since He asks his friends not only to apologize to him but even to ask him to pray for them. Therefore God wished to preserve Job's life and his victories with a spirit of humility.

38.0.8.en: Second: God spoke with Job through the whirlwind and not through angels, as happened with some saints such as Daniel the prophet, or through visions as happened with Ezekiel the prophet, or through dreams as happened with Joseph the righteous, in order to rebuke Job's friends, declaring the honor of this righteous man, that the Lord Himself should come down to him to enter into dialogue with him, a thing for which they themselves had not been made worthy.

38.0.9.en: Third: St. John Chrysostom sees that God covered Job with clouds and storms like one who has come to speak with him from the mercy seat that is upon the lid of the ark of the covenant (Num 7:89).

38.0.10.en: * In my opinion, (God) arranged at that moment that a cloud should cover the righteous man in order to lift up his thoughts and to persuade him that this voice was coming from on high, as in the case of the mercy seat that was upon the ark of the testimony (Num 7:89). For as the cloud is a symbol of heaven, so it is as if God wished to place heaven itself upon Job, and came with His throne drawing near to him. It seems to me that this same thing happened on the mountain when a thick cloud settled there (Ex 19:16), that we might understand that the voice came from on high.

38.0.11.en: St. John Chrysostom Perhaps some ask why the Lord began by rebuking Job and putting to him questions that reveal his weakness in grasping the mysteries of God, His wisdom and His plan, although He had praised him before Satan and had also defended him before his friends. This is God's surpassing love for His believers: though He sometimes stands firm with them even in the midst of their afflictions and trials, yet He defends them before others and prepares for them surpassing glories. He fears for them lest they fall by the sword of pride, but His eyes are upon them; He keeps them, sanctifies them, and glorifies them before His angels and men, and even before Satan.

38.0.12.en: * After the loss of his possessions, the death of his children, the wounds of his body, his wife's words urging him toward evil, the language of abuse directed at him by his comforters, and the arrows of many sorrows that he received with courage, it was fitting that the blessed Job be praised by the Judge for such great strength of endurance, since the time was near for his being called out of this present world.

38.0.13.en: Now the time has come for him to receive double and to regain his former health, so that he might enjoy for a long time the possessions restored to him. Therefore God rebukes with firm justice the one whom He had kept alive, lest through his very victory he perish by the sword of pride.

38.1.0.en: "Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?" [2]

38.1.1.en: It was fitting for Job to shed light on the wisdom of God so that others might come to know it, but instead he spoke of the injustice that had befallen him. Thus God corrects the position of Job, who, although righteous, uttered some words of reproach and so distorted the picture of God's plan before those present.

38.1.2.en: God reproaches him, saying to him: Who are you, who wish to speak about the deep mysteries of God, His justice and His providence? For since you do not comprehend them, you offer a dark interpretation of them.

38.1.3.en: The text in the Septuagint reads: [Who is he that hides counsel from me, and who shuts up words in his heart and thinks to conceal them from me?] The Jesuit translation reads: "Who is this that darkens my justification with words that are nothing of knowledge?" St. Cyril the Great used this expression in his commentary on the Gospel of Luke (Lk 22:64): "And when they had covered him (blindfolded his eyes), they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?"

38.1.4.en: * He says in a certain place through one of His holy prophets: [Who is he that hides counsel from me, and who shuts up words in his heart?] (Job 2:38) He who searches the hearts and minds and is the giver of all prophecy, how could He not know who smote Him (Lk 64:22)? As Christ says: [Darkness has blinded their eyes; and their minds have become blind] (cf. Jn 12:40).

38.2.0.en: St. Cyril the Great * God points to the vast distance that separates us from Him. {Tell me: who is it that tries to hide himself from me, I who know the secrets exactly?!} St. John Chrysostom Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me [3].

38.2.1.en: While God appeared in the whirlwind, before which no man can stand, He asks Job to gird himself like one preparing himself for a work of the utmost gravity (Ex 11:12; 1 Kgs 46:18).

38.2.2.en: The word "man" גֶבֶר here in Hebrew, geber, means a hero. It is as if God says to him: Put away from your mind all fears, and stand courageously as a hero before me. I will present to you a series of questions; when you answer them, you will be answering yourself concerning the questions that you used to set out before your friends about me.

38.2.3.en: As for His saying "gird up... thy loins," or gird yourself: since garments were loose in ancient times, a man had to gird himself in order to run, to work, or to enter battle. To this day most soldiers and commanders gird themselves during war.

38.2.4.en: * When Job fell into a state of discouragement, God turned him back from it with these words.

38.2.5.en: * Girding is part of the soul's journey. Hear what God says to that righteous man: "Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me" (Job 3:38). He says this also to all the prophets. He tells Moses to gird himself. He Himself appeared to Ezekiel (Ezek 11:9) LXX girded. No, and the angels also appear to us girded (Rev 6:15), as soldiers. When we gird ourselves, we also stand courageously, and by our standing we gird ourselves.

38.2.6.en: St. John Chrysostom * The Lord also commanded Job to gird himself, as if it were a kind of sign of maturity (manhood) and readiness for work. He said to Job: [Gird up thy loins like a man] (Job 38:3).

38.2.7.en: St. Basil the Great * In this too St. David boasts that he is girded with the strength of God (Ps 32:18), and he speaks of God Himself as clothed with strength (Ps 1:93), and as girding Himself with His power - against the wicked - although some prefer to see in this a declaration of the abundance of His power, as though it appeared restrained, since He covers Himself with light as with a garment (Ps 2:104). For who can bear His unlimited power and His light?

38.3.s.en: 2. Job's ignorance of how the earth was created

38.3.0.en: 4 Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. 5 Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it? 6 Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; 7 When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

38.3.1.en: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?

38.3.3.en: The first question God puts to him touches the very existence of his own being, as He asks him where he was when God laid the foundations of the earth for his sake. On the one hand, neither Job nor even Adam himself had yet been created; on the other hand, God created the earth for him and for his brothers before they had any existence.

38.3.4.en: Job was not in existence when God founded the earth, and therefore he had no ability to work with God in creation, or to offer counsel, or even to perceive and understand what God was doing for his sake. How then does he dare to complain of God's plan toward him? If Job is unable to understand the laying of the earth's foundations, can he comprehend God's plan and wisdom?

38.3.5.en: * God says: What are you saying? For your sake I founded the earth with such care, would I then neglect him for whose sake I created it...? He utters this to those who demand that He give an account and explanation of events without looking to the loftiness of His wisdom. Who urged me to this? Who advised me? Who came to help me?

38.3.6.en: St. John Chrysostom Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest?

38.4.0.en: Or who hath stretched the line upon it? [5]

38.4.1.en: He asks him: If you know, who set the measures of the earth and determined the dimensions of the equator? Who is the architect who designed the dimensions of the earth? Who held the line to measure it, defining its regions and dimensions?

38.4.2.en: The divine discourse stresses that the earth on which man lives did not come into being by chance without planning, but behind it stands the supreme Architect who laid down a precise plan for its construction; it was created by the wisdom of the Creator and His surpassing power.

38.4.3.en: * The measures were not taken without creativity, nor did it come about by chance or in a random manner, but God designed it with a harmonious purpose, working as a skillful architect.

38.4.4.en: St. John Chrysostom Pope Gregory (the Great) offers us a symbolic interpretation of this phrase, seeing that this earth is the life of man, and that the foundation on which our life stands is firm faith in the fear of the Lord. This faith, with all its measures, is the work of God in us; we may not ascribe it to ourselves.

38.4.5.en: * The foundation of this earth is faith. The foundation of this earth is laid when the hidden places of the heart are marked by the fear of God as the first cause of stability... It is said to Job: Do not ascribe to yourself the virtues that you received from me... So that I may not destroy in you what I have built, you ought not to cease meditating on the state in which I placed you... For we can keep well what we are if we never ignore what we were...

38.4.6.en: Who lays the foundations of this earth but our Creator? He who by the hidden ordering of His inner plan gives to one the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge, to another perfect faith, to another the grace of healing, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another divers kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of sermons... Thus does our Creator and the Orderer of all things act, to keep us from being puffed up by the gift that a person receives, and that he may be humbled by the virtues he has not received... God governs all things thus, so that all receive particular gifts, and all are counted the property of each person individually, through the bond of love. Each one possesses in the other what he himself lacks, and in humility offers to the other what he has received as his own possession. As Peter says: "As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God" (1 Pet 4:10)... And Paul says: "By love serve one another" (Gal 5:13)... And also: "As God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith" (Rom 12:3).

38.4.8.en: "Who hath stretched the line upon it?" Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that those who stretch the line upon the earth to instill the spirit of faith are the preachers, those who cannot work except by God Himself. He gave as an example the Apostle Paul, who neglected to preach in Macedonia, and a man of Macedonia appeared to him in a vision, that he should go and help them (Acts 16:9). And when the Apostle tried to go to Bithynia, he was prevented (Acts 16:7).

38.5.0.en: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof [6]?

38.5.1.en: The discourse here is symbolic, speaking of the creation of the earth as a palace that God built for man the king, digging its foundations and laying a corner stone for the erection of an integral building, strong and exceedingly wide.

38.5.2.en: If the Lord Christ, the incarnate Word of God, or faith in Him, is the foundation on which the new earth, the Church of God, stands, then its bases or the pillars that stand on this foundation are the holy life in the Lord, or the virtues that we practice by the righteousness and grace of Christ, whereby our hearts, our will and all our inner powers are sanctified.

38.5.3.en: Since Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the holy earth the Lord founded is faith, what then are the bases of this earth?

38.5.4.en: * What do we understand by the bases of this earth other than the teachers of the holy Church...?

38.5.5.en: The bases may also refer to the prophets, for when they first spoke plainly of the incarnation of the Lord we saw them as bases resting on the foundation (perhaps he means the Lord Christ, the foundation of faith) and bearing the building that stands upon them...

38.5.6.en: "Or who laid the corner stone thereof?"... It is clear to all who is He whom Scripture calls the corner stone. Truly it is He who took into Himself the Jews on one side and the Gentile people on the other, and united them together as two walls in the building of the Church. It is written, "hath made both one" (Eph 2:14). He showed Himself as the corner stone not only in the lower things but also in the upper, for He united the peoples of the Gentiles with the people of Israel on earth, and united both together with the angels in heaven. For the angels proclaimed at His birth: "On earth peace" (Lk 2:14).

38.5.8.en: "Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the corner stone among those who shout, Honor, honor to it" (Zech 4:7).

38.5.9.en: "Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone" (Eph 2:20).

38.5.10.en: St. Augustine sees that by calling the Lord Christ the head of the corner, who is the head of the Church, the Church thus becomes the corner that joined the Jews on one side and the Gentiles on the other.

38.5.11.en: * It happened on that day which is called His birth that the Jewish shepherds saw Him, while on this day, which should be called "the Divine Manifestation," that is, "the Revelation," the Gentile Magi worshiped Him... Truly He was born as the corner stone for the two, and as the Apostle says: "For to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross" (Eph 2:15-16). What is a corner stone but the joining of two walls of different directions, as though they were exchanging a kiss! The circumcised with the uncircumcised, that is, the Jews with the Gentiles, who bore a common enmity, and had fundamental matters that separated them from one another, for the Jews worshiped the one true God, and the Gentiles worshiped many false gods. The former were near and the latter were far. He led both parties to Himself, He who reconciled them to God in the one body, and as the same Apostle said: and that by the cross, slaying the enmity.

38.6.0.en: St. Augustine When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy? [7]

38.6.1.en: When building a house or a church or some project, a person celebrates with his friends the beginning of digging the foundations and the beginning of laying them.

38.6.2.en: At the beginning of the rebuilding of the Temple [they set the priests in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise the Lord, and they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks unto the Lord; because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the Lord, because the foundation of the house of the Lord was laid] (Ezra 3:10-11). And as the Lord establishes His Church, it is said: "the corner stone shall come forth among those who shout, Honor, honor to it" (Zech 4:7). At the birth of the Lord Christ, the corner stone of the Church of the New Testament, "suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God" (Lk 2:13).

38.6.3.en: What a wonderful picture, as the luminous heavenly orders, the "morning stars," went forth shouting and praising God when they saw the foundations of the earth being laid. Although it was not laid for them, but for man who was to come, and not for them, in love they counted man's happiness their own happiness, and what is offered to him as though it were theirs.

38.6.4.en: God likens Himself to an architect who built a wonderful house, when He created the world, and the heavenly orders rejoiced at this surpassing work. Where was Job at that time?

38.6.5.en: In the seventh chapter of the Conference of Abba Serenus he made clear that God created the heavenly beings before He created the world. "When the stars were made together, the angels praised me with a loud voice" (Job 7:38) LXX. The angels were thus present at the beginning of the creation of the world, praising Him for His works in creating the visible world for us.

38.6.6.en: In a comment by St. John Chrysostom on the signs of the end found in (Mt 29:24), he says that the angels praised the Lord with a loud voice when He created the stars (cf. Job 38:7) LXX. All the more will they praise Him when the final change takes place and the stars fall, since they will no longer be needed, for there is no night in eternity.

38.6.7.en: * All the glorious, unutterable harmony of the heavenly beings above, whether in the service of God or in the common agreement among the heavenly powers, can be preserved by the guidance of the Spirit.

38.6.8.en: St. Basil the Great * Who dares to suppose that the angels were created after the six days of creation? If he is so foolish, his foolishness is removed by Scripture, which has similar authority, where God says: [When I made the stars, the angels shouted to me with a loud voice] (Job 38:7). If the angels existed before the stars - and the stars were created on the fourth day - shall we then say that the angels were created on the third day? God forbid! For we know what was created on that day. The dry land was separated from the waters, every element took its distinctive form, and the earth brought forth everything upon it.

38.7.s.en: 3. His ignorance of setting boundaries for the seas

38.7.0.en: 8 "Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb? 9 When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and the mist a swaddlingband for it, 10 And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors, 11 And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?"

38.7.1.en: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb [8]?

38.7.2.en: Perhaps he refers here to the third day of creation when God said: "Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place" (Gen 1:9).

38.7.3.en: The earth and the deep were mixed together, and when God commanded their separation the waters rushed forth as from the womb of the earth and the seas were formed.

38.7.4.en: The vast seas were formed and became as though shut in with doors or gates from which they do not go out.

38.7.5.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the sea here symbolizes the heart, which man cannot guard or sanctify without divine grace.

38.7.6.en: * What is this sea but our heart, raging in a violent, bitter struggle, swelling with the haughtiness of pride, and darkened with the deceit of evil? How great is the power of its raging waves, a thing understood by him who understands in himself the mystery of the trials of thoughts.

38.7.8.en: * Why does it say "it issued out of the womb" (when it was born)? To show that this took place in stages, and that creation did not come about as by one stroke. It reflects for the hearer what Moses said. As though it had been born, the sea first poured forth, and afterwards took its form and was gathered together into one place (Gen 1:9). So do not think it natural for the sea to be bounded by its shores; rather, God at first allowed the contrary, that the water should exist and spread over the whole surface of the earth.

38.7.9.en: St. John Chrysostom God set boundaries for the primeval sea.

38.8.0.en: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and the mist a swaddlingband for it [9].

38.8.1.en: As He looks at the sea as a newborn child needing clothes and swaddling, God gave it the clouds as a garment covering it, and the mist as a swaddling band to wrap it. Thus God deals with the vast sea as with a little child who needs a nurse to swaddle it and care for it, in spite of its violently raging waves and its sweeping currents.

38.8.2.en: He did not say that He made the mountains and rocks and hills its swaddling band, but He made the mist so, a thing that would never occur to the mind of man.

38.8.3.en: * Do not think that the mist over the waters is a natural thing. He says that it exists by His (divine) command.

38.9.0.en: St. John Chrysostom And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors [10].

38.9.1.en: Lest the sea rage and rebel and destroy man's life on the earth, God bound it by certain limits, and set up for it bars and doors to put limits to its movement.

38.9.2.en: These limits, bars and doors were not set to make the sea lose its ability to fulfill its role or to destroy its mission, but on the contrary, they are for the benefit of the sea itself as well as for the benefit of the earth.

38.9.3.en: God sets for our hearts a divine law or commandment, not to stifle us, nor to deprive us of happiness and freedom, but by this divine commandment we are shaped and return to become in the image of God and to be like Him. This is for our happiness and the happiness of others.

38.9.4.en: The commandment does not confine us as in a prison, but helps our hearts to be enlarged with love toward God and men, even those who oppose us, and we even love all creation, and love our own souls in the Lord.

38.10.0.en: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed? [11]

38.10.1.en: We do not find here anything of the myths that spread anciently, such as the appearance of huge, terrifying sea creatures. Rather, in a wonderful literary and spiritual style, it depicts the sea as though it were born in an atmosphere of calm, having its vital role in interacting with the dry land to serve man. Despite the vastness of the ocean and the violence of the deeps, God set laws that it does not transgress.

38.10.2.en: * Who can tell of the depths of the seas, their vastness and the power of their mighty waves?! And yet they stand at the limits set for them, for it is said: [Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further, and here thou shalt enter, and here shall thy proud waves be stayed]. So the sea clearly shows obedience, for it runs and stands at the shore in a clear line made by the waves, declaring to those who look upon it that it does not transgress the limits set for it.

38.10.3.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem Jeremiah the prophet says: "Fear ye not me? saith the LORD: will ye not tremble at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it: and though the waves thereof toss themselves, yet can they not prevail; though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?" (Jer 5:22). Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus, presents the sea as proof of divine providence.

38.10.4.en: * To persuade you of this, return again to the sea, and observe its depth, its extent, its divisions into bays, its shores, its harbors, the islands in its midst, the kinds of fish in it, their species, forms and variety and their fondness for the shore. Observe the limits of its waves, and the bridle of providence that controls them and keeps them from flooding over the land. When the waves rush upon the sand they keep to the limits, observing the divine law engraved there. They resemble a spiritual horse restrained by its trainer: the waves bow their necks and recede, like one who offers repentance by drawing back when touching the sand.

38.10.5.en: Father Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus * Among the weakest of things is sand, yet the sea cannot resist it in its violence, for it is bridled by it.

38.11.s.en: 4. His ignorance of how the light of dawn emerges

38.11.0.en: 12 "Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place; 13 That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it? 14 It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment. 15 And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.

38.11.1.en: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days?

38.11.2.en: Hast thou caused the dayspring to know his place [12]?

38.11.3.en: God presents Job with perplexing questions so that he may discover his total inability to comprehend the wisdom of God and feel that there is no basis of comparison between his thinking and God's thinking. These questions, although science, with the progress of research, provides answers to some of them, yet the mysteries of nature remain beyond all human thought. What we know scientifically cannot be compared with what we do not yet know.

38.11.4.en: Here he speaks of the first appearance of light at dawn; we are all certain of the existence of light and enjoy it with the dawn until the sun rises.

38.11.5.en: He did not ask him: Is it in your power to hasten the appearance of the dawn and the breaking forth of the light? Rather, he asked him about two matters: whether man was present when the Lord commanded the light to appear, and whether he can determine a place for the dawn. Man was not present when God created the light, and it is not in his power to command the light to shine, nor to determine the place on which it shines. As the psalmist says: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" (Ps 19:1-2).

38.11.6.en: * The heavens (the celestial bodies) obey Him, as they move in peace in subjection to His laws.

38.11.7.en: Day and night they run the course appointed to them, without hindering one another.

38.11.8.en: The sun and the moon with the stars pass through the course appointed to them, according to His command, without any deviation.

38.11.9.en: And the fruitful earth, according to His will, brings forth in due seasons abundant food for man and beasts and all the living creatures that are on the face of creation...

38.11.10.en: The depths (the abyss) that cannot be fathomed, and the indescribable arrangements of the nether world, are subject to the same laws.

38.11.11.en: The sea, immeasurably vast, is gathered together by His work, and does not pass the bounds set for it, but complies with His commands.

38.11.12.en: For He said: [Hitherto shalt thou come, and thy waves shall be broken in thy depths] (Job 38:11).

38.11.13.en: An ocean that man cannot pass over, and worlds that lie beyond it are directed by the will of the Lord.

38.11.14.en: The seasons of spring, summer, autumn and winter succeed one another peacefully, the one after the other.

38.11.15.en: The winds perform their service at the appointed time without hindrance, and the unfailing springs offer their breasts without ceasing as life for men. The smallest of living things come together in concord and peace.

38.11.16.en: All these works the great Creator, Lord of the universe, has ordered, moving in harmony and concord, doing good to all, especially to us, who find refuge in His tenderness, through our Lord Jesus Christ.

38.11.17.en: To whom be glory and majesty for ever and ever. Amen.

38.12.0.en: Pope Gregory (the Great), in his symbolic interpretation, sees that the holy Church is called the dawn because she looks to the reward of the bright heavenly life and abandons the darkness of sin; she is enlightened by the rays of the Sun of righteousness.

38.13.0.en: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth (of the extremities of the earth), that the wicked might be shaken out of it? [13]

38.13.1.en: The dawn is pictured as appearing in the midst of darkness to shine with beautiful colors, so that the works of sinners, who find in the darkness of night an opportunity to practice their dark evils, cease.

38.13.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the extremities of the earth are the humble whom the Lord Christ takes hold of, that is, the fishermen who silence the teachers of the Law.

38.14.0.en: It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment [14].

38.14.1.en: In Egypt, Babylon and Assyria bricks bore a stamp distinguishing the brickworks from one another. Egyptian wine jars and the places where mummies were placed were sealed with a seal on clay. In Assyria some public documents were found with clay stamped with certain letters, distinguishing the official seal. Also the chambers in which treasures were placed were sealed with a seal on clay. Perhaps the tomb of the Lord Christ was sealed thus (Mt 27:66). Clay was preferred to wax because the former grows harder by fire, while the latter melts by it.

38.14.2.en: With every new morning the sun rises on the earth, and it appears illumined as if wearing a new garment; thus the Sun of righteousness imprints His light on His Church, making her a new dawn, enjoying with every morning a new experience in the enjoyment of God's love for her. Thus the image of Christ appears on His Church and His true believers as the seal appears on clay.

38.15.0.en: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken [15].

38.15.1.en: Job had previously spoken of the terror of thieves and criminals at the morning light because it exposes them (Job 24:13). Here God announces the rays of the morning light, that is, the rays of the Sun of righteousness who clothes the true Church with the bright garment of His righteousness, and at the same time deprives the wicked of the light of their joy, and breaks their arm which they lift up against God and men.

38.15.2.en: The light of the Lord Christ, which gives eternal life to His believers, is judgment to those who oppose Him. The Lord Christ Himself says: "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloak for their sin" (Jn 15:22). And the Apostle Paul says: "To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life" (2 Cor 2:16).

38.15.3.en: * To whom then is it "the savour of death unto death" but to those who do not believe, and who are not subject to the Word (Logos) of God...? Again, who are those who are saved and receive the inheritance? Without doubt they are those who believe God and continue in His love, as did Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun (Num 30:14) and the innocent children (Jonah 11:4) who have no sense of evil. But who are those who are saved now, and enjoy eternal life? Are they not those who love God, and believe His promises, and become children in malice (1 Cor 20:14)?

38.16.s.en: 5. His ignorance of perceiving the shadow of death and the darkness

38.16.0.en: 16 "Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth? 17 Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death? 18 Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all. 19 Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof, 20 That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof? 21 Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?

38.16.1.en: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth? [16]

38.16.2.en: He asks him whether he knows what lies hidden in the depth of the sea and the treasures it holds, and whether he can describe the springs of the sea's waters.

38.16.3.en: He returns to the primeval world, and shows the ocean, even if destructive, cooperating with death; so did Job comprehend the secrets of the waters and the secret of death?

38.16.4.en: * He points to Job's confusion: [and in the paths of the dawn (the depth) hast thou walked]. I tell you, not only can you not accomplish one of these works that I have made, but you cannot even know how they were accomplished, nor know or imagine them as they truly are. By these words He was teaching Job of the distance that separates Job and his sons.

38.17.0.en: St. John Chrysostom Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death? [17]

38.17.1.en: Now that He has asked him about matters concerning nature itself, such as the appearing of the dawn, the springs of the sea, and what the sea beds contain, He asks him about a sure matter that touches man's life, namely death, which, as it is said of it, accompanies man from the moment of his birth, and he does not know when it will come upon him. Death remains a riddle in man's life; he does not know when it will come upon him, or by what means, nor can he describe it, nor describe the place to which his soul departs, nor how he lives after death. These are matters that faith offers us and the Creator, the Lover of mankind, reveals to us, although it is a reality that touches the life of every man!

38.17.2.en: Some see that by death he means the place where souls gather after their departure, that is, the kingdom of the dead, or Hades, while the shadow of death points to the very movement of the souls' exodus and departure. These are obscure matters for man, but they are open to God.

38.17.3.en: * Truly, how can we wonder if men have failed with their earthly wisdom to comprehend the mystery of God the Father and of our Lord Jesus Christ, in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Col 3:2), this mystery that the angels could not have known without its being revealed to them!

38.17.4.en: For who can by himself - and not by faith - picture, following the Lord Jesus, how He (the Word) came down from the heights of heaven to the lowest parts of Hades, and behold, He ascends from Hades to the heavens, and at the same time dwells among us without lessening anything of what He was...

38.17.5.en: The angels also stood in marvelous astonishment before the heavenly mystery; thus when the Lord rose, the heights of heaven could not bear the glory of the resurrection from the dead of Him who had at last been confined in the narrow bonds of the tomb, so that the angels were in perplexity...!

38.17.6.en: For the "Conqueror" came adorned with astonishing spoils. The Lord came into His holy temple while angels and archangels went before Him, marveling at those spoils that were set free from death... And by the victory of the Cross - where the rule was upon His shoulders - the spoils were carried to an everlasting victory.

38.17.7.en: He came as though the gates had become too narrow for Him... for they cannot admit His greatness; therefore they sought wider ways and easier passages for the Lord in His return, and thus the Lord lost nothing by emptying Himself (since He returned to His heavenly glory with His spoils).

38.17.8.en: At any rate, they found that a new way must be prepared before the face of this new "Victor," for He is always, as He was, greater than others. But because the gates of righteousness, which are the gates of the Old and New Testaments, in which the heavens are opened, are everlasting gates, therefore they truly do not change, but were lifted up because the one entering is not a man, but the whole world enters in the person of the Savior of all.

38.17.9.en: St. Ambrose Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth?

38.18.0.en: Declare if thou knowest it all! [18]

38.18.1.en: No one had yet gone around the globe, and no man up to that time could know its dimensions, although the earth itself is counted as a point in the midst of the greatness of the whole universe that God created.

38.19.0.en: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof [19].

38.19.1.en: Light succeeds darkness, and darkness light; this is what man observes every day, but does he know the secret of light and the secret of darkness, where they dwell?

38.19.2.en: It is impossible for man to determine a specific place for tangible light and darkness; how then can he comprehend Him who created the light and separated it from the darkness? And what can man know of the light of divine righteousness and the darkness of evil?

38.19.3.en: What man knows is that God is able to turn the heart of man from the darkness of evil to the light of righteousness, but how this is accomplished, this he cannot describe precisely. Every day we touch this work of God, as He shines with the light of His righteousness upon sinners to turn sinners into saints.

38.20.0.en: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof? [20]

38.20.1.en: Man often longs for the rising of the light of day to complete some work, as he longs for the darkness of night to rest from the toil of the day's work, but he does not know where the light of day or the darkness of night goes.

38.21.0.en: Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great! [21]

38.21.1.en: God wished to show the truth about man apart from the sphere of His grace, so He asks Job whether he knows these things, whether his age goes back to the beginning of creation, and he was then born.

38.21.2.en: It is not fitting for man to argue with God about what exceeds his ability, such as the creation of light; rather, in faith he should listen to His divine word: [I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil (chastisements): I the LORD do all these things] (Isa 45:7).

38.22.s.en: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

38.22.0.en: 22 "Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail, 23 Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war? 24 By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth? 25 Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder; 26 To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man; 27 To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth? 28 Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew? 29 Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it? 30 The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.

38.22.1.en: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow?

38.22.2.en: Or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail [22]?

38.22.3.en: After God discussed the subject of creation, He pointed to existing natural phenomena such as the falling of snow, the blowing of winds and the falling of rain. All these God brought into being for the sake of every man. It was fitting for Job to contemplate these wonderful works, which human thought cannot completely define, and which exist for his sake, instead of being occupied with the trials that befall him. There is no basis of comparison between what God permits man of affliction and His divine providence over the whole world for man's sake. It befits the believer that his heart and mind be enlarged to glorify the Creator who ordains everything for his sake.

38.22.4.en: When snow falls in cold countries one is astonished at the countless quantities that fall on whole countries, so that it seems as though the storehouses of heaven had been filled with snow and hail.

38.22.5.en: The inhabitants of regions subject to snow feel God's care for them, and see in the snow precious treasures. For it keeps the earth's warmth so that its temperature does not fall many degrees below zero, and the snow gives fertility to the earth. Therefore, immediately after the snow period, we find the plants in the region that was covered with snow growing with wonderful speed.

38.22.6.en: The Lord uses snow and hail to accomplish His purposes, such as protecting His believers from the raids of the wicked, so He sends down upon them snow and hail on the day of battle, as happened at the time of the Flood when the waters poured out from these storehouses to drown the wicked world, and as He cast great stones from heaven upon the Canaanites (Josh 10:11).

38.22.7.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees in the snow and hail a reference to hearts that are cold in love toward God, as it is said: "the love of many shall wax cold" (Mt 24:12). These hearts the Lord looks upon not with disdain nor in a spirit of anger, but as treasures needing someone to move them. He Himself moved the heart of Saul of Tarsus, who confessed that he had been a blasphemer and a persecutor and a slanderer, and raised him up to be the great Apostle burning with holy zeal.

38.23.0.en: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war? [23]

38.23.1.en: The Lord used these storehouses to chastise the wicked (Ex 9:18; Josh 10:11; Rev 16:21; Isa 28:17; Ps 18:12-13; Hag 2:17).

38.24.0.en: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth? [24]

38.24.1.en: In the phenomenon of thunderclouds the light of lightning appears for moments; but who can describe exactly how the light is emitted, and what its speed is, and what its substance is, and how it quickly dissipates, etc.?

38.24.2.en: Some see that he speaks of the light that issues with the dawn to spread over the earth. Such a phenomenon is simple, which men touch in their daily lives, and yet they do not comprehend its mysteries.

38.24.3.en: He also asks Job whether he understands how the east wind is distributed over the regions. Perhaps he linked light and the east wind in that their source is from the east, and they spread over regions and lands, and he cannot trace their spread.
